details: Check lubricant level/condition and bearing noise/temperature before replacement.
Replace bearing if inspection confirms wear, spalling, seizure, or excessive clearance.

action: Improve suction conditions / verify NPSH margin
details: Check liquid level, suction losses, temperature, valves, and suction piping restrictions.
Inspect impeller surfaces if cavitation persists or performance has degraded.

action: Laser/dial align motor and pump shafts
details: Correct angular/parallel misalignment after verifying soft foot and pipe strain.
Isolate pump and remove deposits or foreign material from impeller passages.
Inspect seal faces, flush plan, elastomers, shaft sleeve, and replace damaged seal parts.

action: Clean suction strainer and inspect suction line
details: Remove blockage; verify suction valve is open and piping is unobstructed.

action: Stop pump and restore prime/liquid supply
details: Do not continue dry operation; restore liquid and investigate why prime was lost.

action: Inspect motor load and process operating point
details: Compare current/load to expected duty; check mechanical drag and process overload.
Check coupling wear, looseness, fasteners, flexible elements, and alignment.
Open pump after isolation; inspect erosion, cracks, blade damage, and clearances.

action: Open/verify discharge valve and minimum-flow path
details: Correct excessive discharge restriction and avoid prolonged near-zero-flow operation.
Tighten fittings/gaskets and inspect suction line for air ingress.

action: Inspect hold-down bolts, soft foot and foundation
details: Tighten/repair base, correct soft foot, and verify grouting/foundation integrity.

action: Check phase voltage/current balance and connections
details: Qualified electrical personnel should inspect phase balance, terminals, and supply.
